newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU seeks 9 pct cut in grain storage increments.
newsitem.headline: EU seeks 9 pct cut in grain storage increments.

text.p: The European Commission proposed on Wednesday to cut by nine percent to 1.0 Ecus a tonne the monthly increases for grain held in intervention stores in 1997/98.
It said in a statement that the proposed reduction was based on interest rate changes.

Cereals intervention prices are raised each month between November and end-May to take account of storage costs and to discourage farmers and merchants from selling into intervention stores at the earliest opportunity. Southern member states have a slightly different schedule.
The Commission also proposed, as part of the 1997/98 (July/June) farm price package, that cereals intervention prices remain unchanged at 119.19 Ecus a tonne.
But it is seeking to cut compensatory payments to cereals farmers by 7.3 percent to 50.37 Ecus tonne.
The Commission's proposals will be presented to EU farm ministers, who are due to take a decision by end-June.
